sources.entry: ntfy - Push notifications to phone or desktop using HTTP PUT/POST, with Android app, CLI and web app, similar to Pushover and Gotify. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) Apache-2.0/GPL-2.0 Go/Docker/K8S
ntfy | Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via simple HTTP requests

summary.one_liner: ntfy is an open-source, HTTP-based pub-sub notification service that lets scripts send push notifications to phones and desktops via simple PUT/POST requests.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes ntfy as a simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service for sending notifications to phones or desktops from scripts on any computer without signing up. It offers a free public instance at ntfy.sh and an open-source Android app (Google Play or F-Droid), plus an open-source iOS app on the App Store. The project can be self-hosted since it is open source, and the README links to docs covering the API, install/self-hosting, and building. The README also mentions a web app, a CLI, and e-mail reception via go-smtp, a persistent SQLite message cache, Firebase (FCM) and webpush-go for push delivery. The README does not give detailed run instructions in the portion provided.
use_cases: send push notifications to my phone from scripts
get alerts on phone or desktop from server jobs
receive HTTP-triggered alerts on Android or iOS
replace Pushover or Gotify style notifications
notable: Send notifications with plain HTTP PUT/POST requests, no signup needed
Free public instance at ntfy.sh plus self-hostable server
Open-source clients for Android (Google Play, F-Droid) and iOS (App Store)
Includes a CLI and a web app
caveats: Paid ntfy Pro plans (from $5/month) are offered for the hosted ntfy.sh service
The README portion provided contains no explicit self-hosting setup steps
summary.license: Apache-2.0 or GPL-2.0 (dual licensed, per README)
